title: SOC2 scratchpad - Maya personal notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for SOC2 scoping and control mapping. NOT a finalized artifact — messy notes, TODOs, and questions to bring to SOC working group.

Scope assumption: Hosted API + Dedicated + Private (VPC package) are in scope for application-level controls; infra (cloud provider) controls will be covered by provider attestations where possible. Clarify with GRC which customers' Dedicated instances are in-scope (committed vs. BYO infra).

High-level control areas to map (brain dump):
- Access management (IAM, admin reviews, SSO, MFA)
- Change management (PR review, release approvals, deployment gating)
- Logging & monitoring (retention, centralized collection, alerting)
- Encryption (at-rest keys, KMS, HSM for Private)
- Incident response (playbooks, sim exercises, postmortems)
- Vendor mgmt (third-party attestations for GPUs, cloud regions)
- Data handling (customer data segregation, deletion, backups)
- Physical & environmental (for any colo-hosted infra customers)

Quick gaps I remember:
- Dedicated: no consistent written runbook for isolated customer failover (owner?) — evidence: none.
- Private (on-prem): need signed customer-local deployment checklist + KMS config matrix.
- Retention: logs retained in hosted for 90 days by default, need mapping to control that requires X months (confirm SOC requirement).

Sample control mapping notes (rough):
1) Access reviews: map to admin-iam-review playbook (CONF-3452), evidence = monthly review spreadsheet + last 3 audit CSVs from Okta. TODO: request export for last 6 months (Arjun).
2) Change mgmt: map to github PR policy + release checklist (PR #892 as example). Need older release approvals archived in Confluence; ask Release Eng for retained approvals (Sofia).
3) Logging/monitoring: centralized ELK/Datadog dashboards + alerting playbooks. Evidence: dashboard screenshots, alert subscriptions list. Question: retention policy for audit logs vs app logs — need an itemized evidence list.

Operational questions / open items (to resolve in WG):
- Which Dedicated customers are considered "in-scope" for SOC2 at first cert? (sales/product input required)
- Do we accept provider SOC reports for GPU cloud infra, or do we need additional controls evidence?
- For Private on-prem installs, what is the minimum set of evidence the customer must provide vs Redwood? (e.g., HSM config screenshots vs attestation)

Actionable next steps (my personal TODO):
- [ ] Pull last 6 months of Okta admin audit CSVs (assigned to Arjun)
- [ ] Compile list of PR approvals for major releases in past year (Sofia to query github org audit logs)
- [ ] Draft a short runbook for Dedicated failover and owner nomination (me + Liam)
- [ ] Create a minimal evidence checklist for Private deployments (Maya to draft, then WG review)

Notes to self: keep this doc informal and time-stamped before copying to shared WG folder. When moving to shared drive, convert loose items into a table: control | owner | evidence | status | notes. For now, use this free-form for brainstorming.

References/anchors I mentioned above: Confluence CONF-3452 (SOC2 overview), JIRA SEC-1123 (evidence collection epic), PR #892 (example of gated release). Slack thread: #security thread for SOC2 kickoff (use for meeting notes).

Unresolved: need clarity from Legal on data retention contractual exceptions (SLA clauses) — add Legal: @Evan Kim to next sync.

End of scratchpad (keeping log of edits): 2026-03-10: added Dedicated failover gap and Private evidence checklist TODO.
